Usar os conectores em pares (entweder …: Use paired connectors (entweder … oder, weder … noch, sowohl … als auch, nicht nur … sondern auch, einerseits … andererseits, zwar … aber, je … desto) to list, contrast and argue.

PASSO 1: um par de conectores liga DUAS: STEP 1: a pair of connectors links TWO matching parts of a sentence — the same pairs English has. «ENTWEDER … ODER» (either … or) gives a CHOICE: «Ich trinke entweder Tee oder Kaffee.» STEP 2: «WEDER … NOCH» (neither … nor) negates both parts; the verb takes NO «nicht»: «Er kann weder lesen noch schreiben» (he can neither read nor write). STEP 3: «SOWOHL … ALS AUCH» (both … and / as well as) adds both: «Sie spricht sowohl Deutsch als auch Englisch.» STEP 4: «NICHT NUR … SONDERN AUCH» (not only … but also): «Ich spreche nicht nur Deutsch, sondern auch Spanisch.» STEP 5: the two parts should be the same type (two nouns, two verbs, two adjectives); the conjugated verb agrees with the subject: with «sowohl … als auch», plural. STEP 6: «entweder … oder» can open the sentence and invert the verb: «Entweder du kommst, oder du bleibst zu Hause.»
o português tem «ou … ou», «nem … nem»,: English has the same pairs: either… or, neither… nor, both… and, not only… but also. German just needs care with the verb position — and remember: "but also" uses «sondern», not «aber».

PASSO 1: «EINERSEITS … ANDERERSEITS» (po: STEP 1: «EINERSEITS … ANDERERSEITS» (on the one hand … on the other hand) shows two sides of an issue: «Einerseits ist das Leben in der Stadt spannend, andererseits ist es laut und teuer.» Both connectors take position 1 (or sit in the middle of the clause); the verb comes right after. STEP 2: «ZWAR … ABER» (admittedly … but) concedes and then counters: «Das Hotel ist zwar teuer, aber es liegt zentral» (the hotel is expensive, it's true, but it's central). STEP 3: «JE … DESTO» (the more … the more) uses the COMPARATIVE in both parts — exactly like English "the more…, the better": the «je» part is a SUBORDINATE clause (verb at the end); the «desto» part is the MAIN clause (verb in 2nd position): «Je mehr ich lerne, desto besser verstehe ich» (the more I study, the better I understand). STEP 4: «je … umso» means the same as «je … desto». STEP 5: use them in opinion texts, in writing and in formal speech.

PASSO 1: uma opinião bem estruturada tem: STEP 1: a well-structured opinion has an INTRODUCTION («Ich möchte über … sprechen» — I'd like to talk about…), ARGUMENTS («Einerseits … andererseits …»), an EXAMPLE and a CONCLUSION («Alles in allem …» — all in all, «Zusammenfassend …» — to sum up). STEP 2: use paired connectors to show both sides and the nuances: «Das Leben auf dem Land hat sowohl Vorteile als auch Nachteile.» STEP 3: for a list with emphasis: «nicht nur … sondern auch». STEP 4: to conclude: «Je mehr ich darüber nachdenke, desto klarer wird es mir» (the more I think about it, the clearer it becomes). STEP 5: remember the difference between «aber» (coordinating, no change in word order) and «sondern» (after a negative): «Ich bin nicht müde, sondern hungrig.»
Stadt oder Land? / Cidade ou campo?: Stadt oder Land? / City or country?
Two colleagues debate where to live.
— Onde você quer morar mais tarde, na ci: — Where do you want to live later on, in the city or in the country?
— Por um lado, a vida na cidade é emocio: — On the one hand, city life is exciting; on the other hand, it's noisy and expensive.
— No campo não é nem barulhento nem caro: — In the country it's neither noisy nor expensive.
— Mas lá há não só tranquilidade, mas ta: — But there you get not only peace and quiet, but also less work.
— Quanto mais tempo moro na cidade, mais: — The longer I live in the city, the more I miss nature.
— Eu poderia ou me mudar para o campo ou: — I could either move to the country or look for an apartment with a garden.
— Tanto a cidade quanto o campo têm vant: — Both the city and the country have advantages.
— That's true. We don't have to decide right now.
